title: parse-playground-debug-journal
content:
Context:
Quick personal lab notes while triaging a recurring parsing failure in user-facing examples for function/tool calling. Repro surface: hosted API, streaming enabled, function schema supplied. Problem: the assistant sometimes emits trailing commas, or partial JSON chunks when streaming ends early, which breaks our parser and causes fallback to text mode. Trying to collect commands, corpus samples, and hypotheses for root cause and short-term mitigations.

Timeline / attempts (ordered newest -> oldest):
2024-11-02 10:14 - live repro on staging with user payload from session id s-1723
- Request: streaming=true, function_call schema: {name: "create_issue", properties: {title: string, body: string, labels: array}}
- Observed: stream ended with final chunk '"labels": ["bug"]}' (ok) in 3/4 runs, but 1/4 runs produced '"labels": ["bug"' (missing closing ]) and connection closed from our side before assistant emitted final ']}' token. Parser raised JSONDecodeError: Unterminated array.
- Raw stream transcript attached in linked_artifacts.

2024-10-28 16:02 - batch test with non-streaming (single full response)
- Request identical except streaming=false. All 50 runs returned valid JSON 50/50. Suggests issue is streaming boundary handling.

2024-10-20 09:31 - forced token truncation test (simulated network drop)
- Intentionally cut connection after N bytes; assistant emitted partial JSON. Behavior: same as field above. Our current parser treats any partial JSON as fatal and falls back to plain-text pipeline which discards structured data.

Commands/quick tests I ran locally (psuedo-CLI):
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{"stream":true, "function_call": "auto", "schema": {..}}' 
- python3 tests/parse_repro.py --session s-1723 --retries 10
- node scripts/stream-collector.js --save transcript.jsonl

Representative broken snippets seen in stream transcripts:
1) ... "labels": ["bug", "priority-high"
2) ... "body": "Steps to reproduce:
1) open X
2) click Y
"
   (then stream terminates abruptly)
3) ... "extra": {"note": "closing brace missing"

Parser errors (Python json module):
- json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 234 (char 233)
- json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting ',', delimiter: line 1 column 311 (char 310)

Immediate hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: The model occasionally flushes partial JSON frames when streaming; our stream-assembler assumes last chunk contains complete object terminator. Need to robustify assembly (buffering, wait short delta for more tokens).
- Hypothesis B: Network interruptions / proxy timeouts cause early socket close; model was still generating; server-side should attempt to emit close-token before TCP FIN. But seeing streaming partials even with stable network.
- Hypothesis C: System message / generation prompt produced stray newlines or unescaped characters (e.g., unescaped \u2028) that make JSON fragile when streamed token-by-token.
- Hypothesis D: Function-calling shim on our side post-processes and inserts extra characters (bug in streaming serializer) when response size > threshold.

Short-term mitigations to implement quickly:
- Parser-level: implement tolerant streaming-JSON assembler that keeps an incremental stack count of braces/brackets; only consider object complete when stack==0 for top-level object AND last token indicates end-of-value (heuristic). If socket closes early, keep transcript and attempt to auto-close with common fixes (append ']}' , '"}', etc) and re-parse. Log as autofix event.
- UX-level: if parsing fails, surface raw transcript to client in error payload so user can see structured data attempt instead of silent fallback to text.
- Model-level: add final sentinel token in schema instructions e.g. "After the JSON response, emit the single line: <<<END-OF-FN>>>" then wait for that sentinel before closing. This is more robust for streaming.

Longer-term investigations/questions:
- Does our streaming TLS proxy ever drop idle connections earlier than backend? Check infra metrics around 2024-11-02 10:14 for proxy resets. (Ping infra team)
- Is the runtime truncating output when exceeding per-request output buffer? Check runtime logs for 'stream_chunk_truncated' or 'emit_error' markers.
- Should we prefer a line-delimited JSON (NDJSON) for function outputs so partial streams can still be parsed line-by-line? Pros/cons: easier incremental parse vs user-visible schema complexity.

Mini experiments to run (next steps):
- A: Add sentinel line and run 500 streaming calls on staging; measure parse success vs baseline. -> low-effort, high-signal. Owner: me. ETA: 1 day.
- B: Implement brace-stack assembler in collector (node + py versions), run against existing transcript corpus, compare auto-fix success. -> medium effort. Owner: Noah. ETA: 3 days.
- C: Turn on verbose runtime stream debug logs in a canary pool and try to reproduce with identical prompt seeds. -> coordinate with Lina (runtime). ETA: 2 days.

Notes / heuristics discovered while poking:
- When model emits long multi-line strings (user-supplied body with line breaks), chunk boundaries frequently break on inside-string boundaries, which can trigger 'Unterminated string' errors. The assembler needs to be string-aware (escape-aware) not just brace counting. 
- Some clients (older SDK versions) treated any final 'non-JSON' characters (e.g., a trailing newline) as fatal. Relaxing parser to call .strip() before json.loads reduced false negatives in non-streamed cases.
- Using JSON5 tolerant parser in collector recovered 12/50 partial transcripts automatically, but JSON5 acceptance of trailing commas risks accepting genuinely malformed structures; flag these auto-accepted cases for manual review.

Scratch ideas for robust protocol variants:
- Double-emit: model emits the JSON object, then emits a checksum line (sha256 of canonical JSON). Collector verifies checksum; if mismatch or missing, mark partial.
- Chunk header: each chunk is prefixed with length and sequence number (in our transport layer) so collector can detect missing chunk(s) instead of assuming generator ended. Requires runtime+transport change.

TODO (me):
- [ ] Create a small reproducible unit test that simulates a JSON string broken in the middle of an escaped quote: e.g. '"long text with a ' inside'
- [ ] Open a runtime issue if we see 'emit_error' markers for the session ids I collected
- [ ] Implement sentinel experiment in a feature branch and share with Noah/Lina for staging run
- [ ] Draft a short note for SDK team about making their streaming parsers more tolerant (examples + recommended heuristics)

Final notes:
- This doc is my running log; keep it rough. If you take on any TODOs, drop a quick note in SLACK:#dev-api so I can coordinate tests.
- If we decide sentinel is the short-term fix, plan to add backward-compatibility flag so older SDKs can opt-in.

End of notes.
